answer: A gale pushed across the open field well before dawn, bending the wheat in long silver waves. I walked to the edge of the grove where the old oaks lean together, and stood still in the cold air listening. Somewhere inside that tangle of roots and shadow a sable slipped past, quick and quiet, leaving only a thin line in the frost. I stayed a while, then turned back toward the house with the wind at my shoulder and the morning slowly filling with light.
